title: One-Pot Cabbage & Tomato Macaroni
description: Tender cabbage and macaroni cook together in a tomatoey broth for a cheap, cozy one-pot dinner.
substitutions: Use small shells instead of macaroni.
Use canned crushed tomatoes instead of diced.
Add a drained can of white beans for extra protein.

steps.text: Simmer the cabbage, pasta, tomatoes, broth, and seasonings together.

cookSteps.text: Combine 4 cups sliced cabbage, 8 ounces elbow macaroni, 1 can diced tomatoes with their juices, 3 cups broth, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a large saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a lively simmer. Cook uncovered for 16–18 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta and cabbage are tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from the heat. Stir in 1/2 cup shredded cheese if using and let stand 2 minutes before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Add a splash of broth when reheating if needed.

title: Ham & White Bean Toast Melts
description: Deli ham and mashed white beans make a fast, filling toast melt with a little cheese on top.
equipment: baking sheet or toaster oven tray

ingredients.item: canned white beans, drained and rinsed

substitutions: Use deli turkey instead of ham.
Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Skip mustard or use mayonnaise if preferred.

steps.text: Top the bread with filling and cheese.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven or toaster oven to 425°F. Mash 1 cup white beans with 1 teaspoon mustard and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, then stir in 3 ounces chopped deli ham.
Divide the mixture over 4 bread slices and top with 3/4 cup shredded cheese.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, until the bread edges are crisp, the filling is hot, and the cheese is melted.

storage: Best fresh. Refrigerate leftover topping separately up to 3 days and assemble before reheating.

title: Leftover Rice & Apple Breakfast Skillet
description: Cold leftover rice warms with apple, cinnamon, and milk into a cozy breakfast that keeps good food out of the trash.
substitutions: Use a pear instead of the apple.
Use white sugar, maple syrup, or honey instead of brown sugar.
Skip the peanut butter or stir in chopped nuts if desired.

steps.text: Warm the rice, apple, milk, sugar, and cinnamon.
Finish with peanut butter if desired.

cookSteps.text: Put 2 cups leftover rice, 1 diced apple, 3/4 cup milk, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon in a medium skillet.
Cook over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until the apple softens and the rice is creamy and steaming hot.
Stir in 1 tablespoon peanut butter if using and serve warm.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat with a splash of milk.

title: Small-Batch Chocolate Banana Bread Pudding
description: Stale bread, one banana, and cocoa turn into a soft chocolate custard dessert sized for a small household.
substitutions: Use white sugar instead of brown sugar.
Add a small handful of chocolate chips if you have them.
Use slightly less sugar for a less-sweet pudding.

steps.text: Put the stale bread in the baking dish.
Whisk and pour over the chocolate-banana custard.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a small baking dish. Put 3 cups stale bread cubes in the dish.

Whisk 1 mashed banana, 1 egg, 1 cup milk, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 2 tablespoons cocoa, 1 tablespoon melted butter, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla if using. Pour over the bread, press gently, and let stand 5 minutes.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the center is set and the top looks lightly dry and baked.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat individual portions gently.
